Review article: using machine learning for snow remote sensing: trends and future directions for global snow measurements
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Snow covers 40 % of Earth’s northern hemisphere each year, playing an important role in regulating Earth’s energy balance through its reflective properties and serving as the primary source of freshwater for one-sixth of the world’s population. Remote sensing is a key technology for observing snow across large areas. Given the complexity of retrieving the snow signal from space, the snow community is increasingly using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches to derive and improve current spaceborne snow measurements. Here we summarize the research trends and applications of ML for snow retrievals, identifying best practices and the future direction of ML applications for multiple seasonal snow-related properties, in particular snow water equivalent (a measurement of the amount of water contained in the snow), snow depth, density, cover, and wet/dry conditions. Across our review, we find that most studies focus on extrapolating to new areas and time periods, with improved prediction after combining multiple sensors and referencing high-fidelity reference data. Gaps remain in generalizing across spatial domains, combining sensors at different spatial and temporal resolutions, and improving the ability of newer model architectures, such as transformers and foundation models, to support snow-related applications. ML/DL for snow remote sensing is an effective tool for integrating information across sensors, and we recommend the snow community continue to identify further use, thereby advancing towards more consistent and complete global snow monitoring that includes a range of snow types and climate conditions.

nodes.name: Reliability and Transferability of Marine Harmful Algal Bloom Detection Using Ocean-Color Satellite Observations: From Optical Signals to Trustworthy Products
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Satellite ocean-color remote sensing is used to detect harmful algal blooms (HABs), yet detection capability does not necessarily ensure reliable interpretation or transferable performance. If these limitations are overlooked when developing cross-regional or global automated HAB early-warning systems, biological claims may be overstated and regional changes in false-alarm or missed-detection rates may go unnoticed, potentially compromising warning reliability and related management decisions. We develop an evidence-constrained framework to evaluate both dimensions: reliability, defined by whether the observation–processing–inference chain supports the intended biological claim, and transferability, defined by whether task-relevant performance is retained under changes in time, region, sensor, or optical environment. A structured Web of Science search yielded 1212 unique records, from which 28 purposively prioritized full-text core studies underwent coding for validation design, cross-domain evidence, error, and uncertainty. The synthesis identifies an evidentiary gap between optical detection capability and biological claim specificity, while fixed-configuration cross-domain evidence was scarce and performance retention remained unquantified. Satellite observations can support bloom presence, optical phenotypes, and selected taxon-targeted applications, but specific claims require specific independent biological references. Reliability is constrained by reference and labeling practices, preprocessing, observation availability, and incomplete uncertainty characterization, while evidence for transferability is limited by insufficient source–target evaluation. We propose a framework linking claim–evidence alignment, independent validation, domain-shift assessment, and uncertainty reporting. Reliable and transferable HAB remote sensing should move beyond detection outputs toward evidence-supported, uncertainty-aware products for monitoring, early warning, and decision-making.

nodes.name: RSFAKE-1M: A Large-Scale Dataset for Detecting Diffusion-Generated Remote Sensing Forgeries
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology
nodes.abstract: Detecting forged remote sensing images is critical for maintaining trust in environmental monitoring and national security. While diffusion models have enabled highly realistic forgeries, their impact on forensic systems remains underexplored due to the lack of adequate benchmarks. Existing datasets are typically small-scale and GAN-centric, failing to represent the complexity of modern generative models. To bridge this gap, we introduce RSFAKE-1M , a comprehensive million-scale benchmark containing 500K real and 500K forged images. It captures a wide spectrum of forgery traces by incorporating samples from ten distinct diffusion models under six diverse generation conditions (e.g., text-to-image, inpainting). To demonstrate the benchmark's utility and explore new detection paradigms, we conduct a systematic evaluation of existing detectors and introduce RSFAKE-bench , an exploratory MLLM-based baseline that utilizes token probabilities to derive a continuous detection score. Our extensive experiments on RSFAKE-1M reveal the limitations of current specialized detectors in cross-generator generalization, while the MLLM-based exploration indicates that RSFAKE-bench can additionally provide human-readable reasons describing geographic and physical inconsistencies for its judgments. We release RSFAKE-1M to serve as a foundational resource for developing and rigorously evaluating next-generation forensic solutions. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TZHSW/RSFAKE/ .

nodes.name: Persistent Urban Heat Analysis from Multi-Satellite Observations Using Machine Learning
nodes.venue: Climate
nodes.abstract: Annual land surface temperature (LST) products are widely used to characterize urban heat, but absolute temperatures combine local surface variation with broader differences among cities and years. This study evaluates AlphaEarth annual satellite embeddings for predicting absolute LST and city-year median-centered thermal anomalies across seven cities from 2017 through 2025. A predictor comparison evaluated the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI), their combination, Landsat surface reflectance, and AlphaEarth embeddings using Random Forest regression. AlphaEarth achieved R2 = 0.812 and RMSE = 2.99 °C for absolute LST prediction and R2 = 0.648 for median-centered anomalies, outperforming conventional predictors. Spatial and temporal validation demonstrated strong recovery of local thermal structure, although transfer to previously unseen cities was weaker. Fixed-location analysis showed strong agreement in multiyear mean anomalies (r = 0.914) but limited recovery of interannual variability (r = 0.096). Geographic reconstruction across seven cities further demonstrated the ability to represent persistent spatial thermal patterns, with greater agreement for mean anomalies than warm-decile recurrence. A supplementary Local Climate Zone (LCZ) analysis associated compact built environments with higher relative surface temperatures and greater hot-tail prevalence, while vegetated environments exhibited cooler conditions. These findings demonstrate the value of AlphaEarth embeddings for characterizing urban surface thermal structure while identifying limitations in temporal variability and geographic transfer.

nodes.name: Onboard AI-Driven Autonomous Tasking for Rapid Wildfire Response with a LEO Wide-Swath Observation Satellite
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) remote sensing satellites exhibit significant limitations in emergency response operations, primarily due to the constraints of orbital mechanics and a traditional reliance on ground-involved, open-loop operational models. Current response latencies often span several hours, rendering acquired data less effective for disasters with rapid temporal dynamics. We propose a new intra-pass autonomous reaction application mode to solve this key problem in emergency response. We build the mode on an agile satellite platform operating in an 800 km sun-synchronous orbit. We equip the platform with two core sensors through an innovative design. The two sensors are an optical camera with 0.5-meter resolution and a forward-looking infrared camera. The infrared camera has a 600-kilometer swath and a 10-meter nadir resolution. We take onboard artificial intelligence technologies as the research core. The technologies support real-time and autonomous analysis of forward-looking infrared image data. This analytical capability facilitates the real-time detection and autonomous confirmation of stochastic events, such as wildfires, by leveraging onboard artificial intelligence (AI) to perform real-time analysis of IR imagery. This subsequently triggers immediate autonomous re-tasking for high-resolution follow-up observation within the same orbital pass. We establish an optimization model for the satellite system. The model is used to solve the key balance problem between the sensor forward-looking angle, achievable reaction time, and actual detection resolution. We conduct a detailed engineering time budget analysis for the whole satellite operation system. Analysis results show that a specific forward-looking angle must be set for the infrared camera to obtain a 70-second autonomous response window of the satellite. The 70second window contains 30 seconds for AI cognitive analysis, a maximum of 33.6 seconds for platform attitude maneuvering, and 10 seconds for platform stability adjustment. The minimum forward-looking angle required for the infrared camera is about 33.6 degrees. The ground sampling distance of the infrared camera will decrease to 12.2 meters at this angle. The resulting 12.2-meter ground sampling distance (GSD) remains sufficient to meet the practical requirements of early-stage detection. The proposed Intra-Pass Autonomous Reaction (IPAR) mode reduces emergency response times from hours to seconds, significantly enhancing the proactive observation capabilities of LEO platforms.

nodes.name: Nanosecond pulsed laser coloring technology based on deep learning
nodes.venue: Twenty-First National Conference on Laser Technology and Optoelectronics
nodes.abstract: Nanosecond laser coloring offers significant advantages in corrosion resistance, abrasion resistance, and environmental friendliness. However, accurate prediction and control of coloration effects remain challenging due to the complex, nonlinearly coupled processing parameters. Herein, we propose a deep learning-based framework for both forward and reverse modeling of laser coloration on stainless steel. A dataset comprising 1620 parameter-color pairs was established using a home-built nanosecond laser system. A forward fully connected neural network was trained to map laser parameters to color values, achieving a prediction accuracy above 0.95; notably, the predicted colors exhibit excellent visual and quantitative agreement with the experimental actual colors. For color-driven parameter retrieval, a reverse neural network was constructed. Although the processing parameters predicted by the reverse network deviate substantially from the actual experimental values, feeding these predicted parameters back into the forward model yields a color prediction accuracy of approximately 0.98. This demonstrates that the reverse model can effectively approximate the equivalent solution space of the laser coloring process. Additionally, two self-developed image processing algorithms were specially self-developed for automatic shape correction and rapid color extraction. This work establishes a viable and robust technical pathway for intelligent, customized laser coloration.

Multi-hazard road-network criticality from earth observation data using spatial graph attention networks with conformal uncertainty
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Coastal deltaic road networks in India experience compounding hazards of monsoon flooding, prolonged soil-moisture saturation, and heat stress. However, many graph-learning approaches to network vulnerability assessment validate with random train–test splits that do not account for spatial dependence between adjacent road segments leading to insufficient quantification of failure probability without any spatially calibrated uncertainty. This study attempts to address these gaps by developing a spatially aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) that estimates road-segment failure probability from multi-hazard exposure and network-topological covariates. Due to the lack of geocoded road-closure records, multi-hazard threshold rules were used to generate training labels, with model predictions interpreted as disruption susceptibility rather than observed failure probabilities. Model performance was evaluated using random and spatial-block cross-validation, while split-conformal prediction was used to quantify predictive uncertainty. The framework was applied to the East Godavari–Krishna deltaic corridor of coastal Andhra Pradesh using multi-source climate, satellite, terrain, road-network and population data (i.e., IMD, NASA SMAP, ERA5-Land, CHIRPS, Copernicus DEM, Sentinel-2, OpenStreetMap, and WorldPop) from 2016 to 2025. The GAT achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.923 ± 0.001 under random cross-validation, and 0.682 ± 0.126 under spatial-block cross-validation. Under spatial-block cross-validation, Random Forest outperformed the GAT in all five folds, achieving an AUC of 0.746 ± 0.134 using the same edge-level features without network topology. Message-passing ablation indicated a marginal improvement from real network topology, with an AUC of 0.639 without message passing compared with 0.624 using randomly shuffled neighbours. A population-weighted Monte Carlo simulation showed that failure-probability-weighted removal produced greater network efficiency loss than random removal across all tested removal fractions (1%–20%), with the largest difference observed at 10% removal, where the loss ratio reached 1.65 times. A consequence-sensitive risk ranking combining failure probability and demand-weighted network flow identified a top 5% of segments whose protection avoided 56% of simulated accessibility loss, compared with 15% for failure-probability ranking, 18% for hazard-exposure ranking, and 43% for edge betweenness.

nodes.name: Mechanobiology of osteoarthritis: from mechanical-dose sensing to organelle homeostasis and the emerging concept of mechanical memory
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
nodes.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous whole-joint disease in which mechanical, inflammatory, metabolic, and age-related factors converge to disrupt tissue homeostasis. Mechanical loading is essential for cartilage maintenance, whereas excessive or insufficient mechanical stimulation may disrupt cartilage homeostasis depending on the loading modality, magnitude, frequency, duration, recovery conditions, and tissue context. In this review, we integrate OA mechanobiology across scales, from whole-joint load redistribution and tissue-level mechanical filtering to chondrocyte mechanosensing and intracellular responses. The mechanistic emphasis is on cartilage and chondrocytes within the broader whole-joint context of OA. We discuss how integrin-focal adhesion complexes, PIEZO1/2, TRPV4, primary cilia, the cytoskeleton, and nuclear mechanotransduction regulate matrix metabolism, mitochondrial redox homeostasis, autophagy and mitophagy, regulated cell death, and cellular senescence. We further highlight mechanical unloading, immobilization, and microgravity-related models as distinct experimental contexts and discuss epigenetic, epitranscriptomic, and ubiquitin-dependent regulation as potential mechanisms underlying persistent cellular reprogramming, while recognizing that mechanical memory after stimulus withdrawal remains insufficiently established in OA. Finally, we outline how subject-specific modeling, spatial multi-omics, joint-on-chip systems, and multimodal mechanical phenotyping may support mechanobiology-guided OA stratification and therapy. Restoring patient-specific mechanical homeostasis, rather than simply reducing loading, may provide a framework for precision management of OA.

Mask2Former–FGMBRM: A Feature-Guided Building Segmentation Framework for Automated 3D Urban Environment Generation from Satellite Imagery
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Building-footprint errors can propagate into geospatial assets generated from remote-sensing imagery. This study evaluated Mask2Former–FGMBRM, which applies feature-guided residual refinement to Mask2Former query-mask predictions and integrates extracted footprints with documented terrain data and geospatial processing for footprint-based urban asset generation. Six models were evaluated on 518 WHU held-out images using common final references and metric definitions while retaining model-specific pipelines. The tune-selected Mask2Former baseline and FGMBRM achieved AP values of 72.03% and 73.49%, respectively, a 1.47-percentage-point improvement. FGMBRM also achieved 89.01% binary IoU and 91.86% object F1, leading these measures and AP among the six configurations, whereas SegFormer had the highest boundary F1. Controlled ablations showed metric-dependent trade-offs, with simpler variants leading selected outcomes and no consistent advantage from query-conditioned guidance. The original INRIA comparison remained limited. In a separate query-capacity diagnostic, AP at common maxDets = 100 increased from 20.66% to 23.96%, while retaining more outputs increased recall and false positives. The results support footprint-based urban asset generation and visualization, with remaining dense-scene and geometric limitations.

nodes.name: Integrating Dual-Stream Coordinate and Cross-Spatial Attention for Drone-View Traffic Detection
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract:
Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are essential for traffic monitoring in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). However, the detection of traffic objects in drone-view imagery still faces serious challenges due to drastic scale variations, dense small objects, and complex background clutter. Existing detectors often struggle to effectively separate targets from background noise and lack efficient cross-scale feature interaction mechanisms. This paper introduces ED-DETR, a refined real-time Detection Transformer specifically designed to optimize performance in UAV scenarios.
Specifically, a Dual-Stream Coordinate Attention (DCA) module is designed, which can effectively extract significant texture features while preserving context information through parallel maximum pooling and average pooling operations. In addition, this paper introduces an efficient multi-scale attention structure in the feature fusion neck, which combines grouping convolution and cross-spatial learning to significantly improve the positioning ability of small targets. A large number of experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset show that ED-DETR achieves an mAP of 40.4%, which is significantly higher than that achieved by RT-DETR and other state-of-the-art detectors. By harmonizing high detection accuracy with low computational overhead, the proposed framework enables effective real-time monitoring of aerial traffic scenarios.

nodes.name: Hierarchical cross-temporal frequency network for remote sensing building change detection
nodes.venue: Journal of Applied Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Building change detection (BCD) using remote sensing images has become a crucial technique for urban planning. Although deep learning-based methods for BCD have made significant progress in the field of remote sensing imagery, they still encounter several challenges, including unclear detection of boundaries of buildings, susceptibility to noise interference, and missed detection of subtle changes. To address these issues, we propose a hierarchical cross-temporal frequency network (HCTFNet) to achieve more precise and refined building change detection. Specifically, we design a frequency-channel enhancement model, which incorporates a frequency-guided spatial attention block to capture different frequency components of input features, thereby enabling more accurate extraction of textural details and building edges, and a residual channel attention block to assign weights to features from a channel-wise perspective, which suppresses invalid channel features and enhances the model’s capability to detect change regions. We further introduce a cross-attention fusion block to establish spatial correlations between the two temporal phases, strengthen the representation of change regions, and fuse the features to highlight areas with the most significant changes. Experimental results show that HCTFNet achieves F1-scores of 92.10% on the LEVIR-CD dataset, 89.58% on the WHU-CD dataset, and 80.10% on the SYSU-CD dataset, outperforming most of the existing mainstream change detection methods.

nodes.name: Grounded Reasoning for Visual Ambiguity Resolution
nodes.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
nodes.abstract: In this paper we seek to correct errors and ambiguities in visual perception by opportunistically applying metacognitive symbolic reasoning. In particular, we present a system which uses a confidence threshold to gate visual reasoning -- confident perceptions are left untouched while ambiguous perceptions are passed to a reasoning engine. This framework deploys a modular, dual-process pipeline where fast, purely neural perception is optionally followed by a reasoning phase which leverages paraconsistent logic for ambiguity resolution. By extracting bounding boxes alongside object detections, the system transitions from basic propositional logic to location-based predicate reasoning, allowing it to evaluate spatial configurations. To demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, we run several experiments comparing purely neural visual reasoning against hybrid propositional and hybrid first-order logic frameworks. Across datasets requiring varying degrees of spatial precision, ranging from detecting check states on a chessboard to identifying contextual tells in train images, our findings illustrate that predicate grounding reduces perceptual ambiguity and outperforms propositional baselines.

nodes.name: Fixed-Prototype Spatial Voting for Visual Sea-State Classification
nodes.abstract: Wepresent a 24,984-parameter sea-state classifier trained through recurrent refinement and deployed by direct spatial voting. Across ten archived encoders, voting averages 85.79% accuracy versus 85.65% with recurrence. A selected archived checkpoint with a floating-point encoder and latent-INT8 voting achieves 89.02%, versus MUSeNet’s published 88.7%, at approximately 1/80 of its parameters. Packing preserves the integer vote in 196 bytes. Instructioncycle accounting bounds the voting head at 182.5 µs on a 16-MHz ATmega328P; the encoder requires 23.71 million multiply–accumulate operations per image. A supporting Otter USV simulation links edge-processing budgets and ordinal recognition errors to supervisory response.
